description: Adds or removes a known clothing item from the user's personal wardrobe by its style ID. Use this tool when users want to track clothing items they own or indicate they have something similar. Use cases: "Add this to my wardrobe", "I have a similar jacket", "Mark that I own this", "Remove this from my wardrobe". Requires authentication - if user is not logged in, this will trigger an OAuth authentication flow. Wardrobe items are used to personalize outfit suggestions with clothes the user actually owns. IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, look at the structured output of the most recent suggest-outfit-tool call earlier in this conversation. The styleId required by this tool is at outfitItems[i].styleIdentifier.styleId in that result — it IS present in your context. Do not claim you cannot see the styleId without first examining that tool result. If after examining it you still cannot find a matching item, tell the user and ask them to request a new outfit suggestion first.

addOrRemove.description: The action to perform: "add" to include the item in the user's wardrobe, or "remove" to delete it from their collection. Use "add" when user says "I have this shirt" or "Add the shoes to my wardrobe". Use "remove" when user says "I don't have the pants anymore" or "Remove the sneakers from my wardrobe".

categoryName.description: Provide the category name of the style to add to or remove from the wardrobe. For example: "Jackets", "Shirts", "Trousers", "Shoes". This value is provided in outfit suggestion responses in the "category" field.

isUserStyle.description: Whether this is a user-created custom style (true) or a catalog style from the platform (false). Most items from outfit suggestions will be catalog styles (false). IMPORTANT: This value MUST be copied exactly from the `styleIdentifier.isUserStyle` field returned in the most recent previous `suggest-outfit-tool` response. Do NOT guess this value.

styleDescription.description: The user-friendly description of the style to add to or remove from the wardrobe. IMPORTANT: This value MUST be copied from the `description` field of the outfit item returned in the most recent previous `suggest-outfit-tool` response.

styleId.description: The unique identifier of the clothing style/item. IMPORTANT: This value MUST be copied exactly from the `styleIdentifier.styleId` field returned in the most recent previous `suggest-outfit-tool` response. You DO have access to previous tool responses. They are in JSON format. Review the tool call responses earlier in the conversation to find the correct styleId to use here and look for the most recent one from `suggest-outfit-tool`. Do NOT fabricate, guess, or invent this value. Once you think you have it, double-check the most recent suggest-outfit-tool response to confirm you are using the correct value from the context. If no valid styleId is available from a prior `suggest-outfit-tool` response, do not call this tool — instead tell the user that you need to suggest an outfit first before you can add an item to their wardrobe. If no item from the prior outfit suggestion seems to match what the user is describing, you can ask the user for more details about the item they want to add or remove, and then use that information to determine if any of the items from the prior outfit suggestion are a match.  But you should never guess or make up a styleId.

name: add-to-or-remove-from-wardrobe-by-id

altText.description: Accessible description of the style image.

embedded.description: Whether the same image is included as a standard MCP image content block.

mimeType.description: Image MIME type when it was verified during embedding, otherwise null.

url.description: Short-lived URL for the added or removed style image.

image.description: The added or removed style image details when available, otherwise null.

styleId.description: The identifier of the style that was added or removed. Absent or null if there was a problem.

text.description: A message summarising the outcome of the wardrobe update to display to the user. Always populated, including on failure.

toggleConfirmed.description: True when the wardrobe update was successfully applied. Absent if there was a problem.

type.description: The action that was performed. Absent if there was a problem.

warnings.description: Non-fatal limitations, such as an image that could not be embedded.
